    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id

           MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase,
           COUNT(*) AS order_count,
           -- Keep every delivered order, but do not treat a missing payment as zero.
           CASE WHEN COUNT(p.paid_cents) = COUNT(*) THEN SUM(p.paid_cents) END AS spend_cents
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_spend AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
rfm_values AS (
    SELECT customer_totals.*,
           -- Calendar days from the customer's last delivered purchase to the latest
           -- delivered purchase in the dataset; purchases on that last date have R-days = 0.
           CAST(julianday(date(MAX(last_purchase) OVER ())) - julianday(date(last_purchase)) AS INTEGER) AS recency_days
    FROM customer_totals
),
scores AS (
    -- Score by cumulative percentile: (0,20%] = 1, ..., (80%,100%] = 5.
    -- Equal values receive the same score, even if the quintiles are unequal in size.
    SELECT rfm_values.*,
           CEIL(5 * CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY recency_days ASC)) AS r,
           CEIL(5 * CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY order_count DESC)) AS f,
           CASE WHEN spend_cents IS NOT NULL THEN
               CEIL(5 * CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY (spend_cents IS NULL) ORDER BY spend_cents DESC))
           END AS m
    FROM rfm_values
),

           CASE

               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'Can''t Lose Them'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 'Hibernating'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'Lost'
               WHEN r IN (2, 3) AND f + m BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Loyal Customers'
               WHEN r = 3 AND f + m BETWEEN 5 AND 6 THEN 'Needs Attention'
               WHEN r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 8 THEN 'Recent Users'
               WHEN (r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 5 AND 6)

               WHEN r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Price Sensitive'
               WHEN r = 2 AND f + m BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Promising'
               WHEN r = 3 AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'About to Sleep'
           END AS rfm_segment
    FROM scores

           spend_cents / (100.0 * order_count) AS customer_avg,

    SELECT i.product_id, '2018-12-01', i.qty, p.qty_minimum, p.qty_purchase
    FROM inventory_totals AS i
    JOIN product_minimums AS p ON p.product_id = i.product_id

    UNION ALL

    SELECT r.product_id, b.mth,
           r.ending_qty - b.qty
               + CASE WHEN r.ending_qty < r.qty_minimum THEN r.qty_purchase ELSE 0 END,
           r.qty_minimum, r.qty_purchase
    FROM projection AS r
    JOIN monthly_budget AS b
      ON b.product_id = r.product_id
     AND b.mth = date(r.mth, '+1 month')
    WHERE b.mth < '2020-01-01'
), differences AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, ABS(ending_qty - qty_minimum) AS absolute_difference
    FROM projection
    WHERE mth >= '2019-01-01'
), ranked AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, absolute_difference,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY absolute_difference, mth
           ) AS rn
    FROM differences
)
SELECT product_id, mth AS month, absolute_difference
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY product_id;

    UNION ALL
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, constructor_id, points FROM sprint_results

    SELECT r.year, p.driver_id, p.constructor_id,

    FROM event_points AS p
    JOIN races AS r ON r.race_id = p.race_id

), ranked AS (

    FROM scoring_drivers
)

FROM ranked
JOIN constructors AS c ON c.constructor_id = ranked.constructor_id
WHERE ranked.points_rank = 1
GROUP BY c.constructor_id, c.name
ORDER BY season_count DESC, c.name ASC
